Thank you, LGS community! We're incredibly grateful for the fantastic response to our Pre-Loved Uniform donation campaign. Thanks to the generosity of our families, we've received a wonderful collection of high-quality uniform that will help support other members of our school community. Although our Donation Fortnight has now ended, we're pleased to let you know that we'll continue to accept clean, good-quality uniform donations at Reception throughout the year. We're now busy sorting and preparing everything ready for the Pre-Loved Uniform Shop. Details of upcoming sale dates and other opportunities to purchase items will be shared very soon, so keep an eye on our social media and school communications. Thank you for helping us make school uniform more affordable, reduce waste and support our LGS community. #lgsconfident
Langley Grammar School Students Perform with Slough Youth Orchestra at the Reading Hexagon. On Monday 22nd June, Langley Grammar School students performed with Slough Youth Orchestra and the Slough combined choir at the Reading Hexagon as part of a large-scale concert involving over 40 schools from across Slough, conducted by our very own Mr Batsman. The event brought together a combined choir of more than 200 pupils, alongside the orchestra, creating a powerful celebration of music across the borough. The orchestra performed a varied programme, including The Planets by Gustav Holst, Pure Imagination from Willy Wonka and the Chocolate Factory, and an exciting mash-up of Oh When the Saints and Hallelujah Chorus. A significant number of students in the orchestra were from Langley Grammar School, which was wonderful to see and reflects the strength of music across the school. Our students performed with real confidence, focus and professionalism throughout the event. Many audience members and staff commented on the high standard of their playing and singing, both in the orchestra and as part of the combined choir. This concert was a fantastic example of the power of music to bring young people together. It also demonstrated exactly why Langley Grammar School is proud to be a Lead School for Music in Slough, supporting high-quality musical opportunities and helping students to develop confidence, teamwork and a lifelong appreciation of music. We are incredibly proud of all the students involved, and thank you to all the staff who supported throughout the project, including Mr Batsman, Mr Wilkinson, Ms Kenner, Ms Douthit and all the staff from Slough Music Service. Look out for future Slough Youth Orchestra Concerts in the very near future. #lgsconfident

Overview of Careers Provision
We take pride in the consistent evaluation of our careers provision, ensuring that we proactively seek to respond to the needs of our students. As a result, each year group have a scheduled calendar of careers interactions which are closely aligned with the Gatsby benchmarks.
The below overview places a focus on each year group, outlining what students can expect to experience as part of their careers education and work-related learning programme in each academic year. In addition to the overview below, students also benefit from additional one-off events and activities such as visiting speakers, competitions and online events, as and when opportunities arise. Many of these are promoted through our LGS Futures bulletin as well as our Sixth Form newsletter.

Our Careers Team meet regularly in order to discuss progress and reflect on the effectiveness of our programme, ensuring that any adaptations are made with clear strategy and intention.

Music Lessons
Langley Grammar School has a very active and flourishing Music department. As well as offering music within the school curriculum, specialist instrumental and vocal tuition is available on a wide range of instruments with our highly skilled and accomplished peripatetic music staff. These sessions take place during school hours on a rotation system to minimise disruption. Prices are competitive. Currently, there are around 200 students learning a musical instrument at the school.

LGS Futures: Careers & Higher Education
Introduction
Young people today have more choice about what to do in the future than ever before. At Langley Grammar School, we prepare students for the challenges and opportunities of adult life through a progressive programme of careers-related activities designed to develop the skills, attitudes and knowledge needed to be successful in the world of work in the 21st Century.
Additional information and advice is offered through these website pages and the Careers Library located in the school’s Library. This information is updated routinely throughout the year with a full review annually, which is conducted in the Autumn Term and completed by 20 December each year. As well using the information on these website pages, parents, students and employers are welcome to contact our key staff below for further information about our careers programme.
Key staff
The school's Careers Leader is Miss Yasmin Padwal. She may be contacted through the main school phone number 01753 598300 or via the school email address school@lgs.slough.sch.uk marked for the attention of the Careers Leader.
The school contracts with David Ritchie & Associates for the provision of specialist careers advice and guidance. Our attached careers and HE advisor is Mr Sailesh Devani, who is based in the school for three days each week. Mr Devani supports all students throughout their time at school. All students in Years 11-13 are offered a 1:1 guidance interview to help them make decisions about A Level and University courses; alternatives such as vocational courses and apprenticeships, and future career planning. Mr Devani also works with younger students in Years 7-10 to help them explore the world of work and further education.
Employers
If you are an employer and are interested in supporting our careers provision, for example, by attending our annual careers fair or providing us with information about the opportunities you offer, please contact the school's Careers Leader, Miss Yasmin Padwal, via school@lgs.slough.sch.uk or 01753 598300.
Education and training providers
We believe that all students should have the opportunity to explore what it is like to learn at the full range of learning providers, including colleges, universities, apprenticeship and training providers (including employers), University Technical Colleges (UTCs) and Studio Schools. If you are such a provider and interested in coming into the school please refer to our Provider Access Statement on our Policies page here for further details.
Careers policy
The school's policy statement on Careers Education, Information, Advice and Guidance can be found on our Policies page here.

Langley Grammar Students celebrate fantastic A-Level results
Congratulations to students at Langley Grammar School, who are once again celebrating an excellent set of A-Level results after two years of hard work, dedication and perseverance.
This year, more than 82% of A-Level entries achieved grades A*, A or B. These impressive results have helped students secure places at leading universities and degree-level apprenticeships. Eighteen students gained three or more A* grades, which is a fantastic achievement.
Headteacher David Harding said: “We are immensely proud of everything our students have achieved in their A-Level examinations. Their excellent results are a testament to the commitment, determination and effort they have shown throughout the past two years. I would also like to thank our staff for the outstanding teaching, support and guidance they have provided, which have played such an important part in these achievements.”

Excellent GCSE results for LGS students
Congratulations to students at Langley Grammar School who are celebrating another year of superb GCSE results.
This year, over 77% of GCSE entries were awarded grades 7-9. The average grade achieved was 7.5. The overall pass rate at grade 4 or above was 99.8%, the highest achieved by the school since the introduction of the 9–1 grading system. There were also some outstanding individual performances, with thirteen students achieving at least nine grade 9s
These outstanding results are a reflection of the hard work of our students and dedication of our staff.
Headteacher, David Harding, commented, ‘We are hugely proud of what our students have achieved. These excellent GCSE results are a real testament to their determination, effort and ambition, and will open the door to the next stage of their education and beyond. It has been a pleasure to celebrate today and to see the students’ hard work rewarded. I would also like to thank our staff for their dedication, expertise and support, and our families for the encouragement they have given over the last five years.’

Parents
"Parents and pupils appreciate how the school expects pupils not just to excel in the more traditional academic subjects, but to broaden their horizons through creative, artistic and sporting subjects."
Ofsted, November 2021
Strong positive relationships with parents are key to our students' success. We seek to work in partnership with parents to support their sons and daughters throughout their time at Langley Grammar School.
Effective two-way communication between the school and parents is very important. These website pages contain useful information for parents, and we would encourage you to contact us if you have questions or concerns so we can put you in touch with the right member of staff.
As part of an effective partnership we do expect parents to fully support the ethos and values of the school. We do not regard ourselves as an 'examination factory' - we believe in the development of confident and well-rounded young men and women for whom academic success is balanced with a broad outlook and a range of other interests. We look to parents to actively promote the personal development of their sons and daughters alongside their academic progress.

Curriculum
At Langley Grammar School our curriculum is shaped by our school ethos of supporting students in becoming confident and well-rounded, independent and creative, responsible and caring.
We have two main and overlapping aims for our curriculum:
First, as a grammar school with able students we seek to deliver an enjoyable, engaging and challenging academic curriculum, which is also broad and balanced, that develops students’ subject specific knowledge, understanding and skills, which will equip them well for further academic study and the workplace.
Second, our curriculum supports students’ wider personal development, so that they can develop the skills, attributes and cultural awareness to thrive as individuals, citizens and members of communities in their adult lives.
In relation to the first aim we seek to develop subject specific knowledge by:
1. Subject areas identifying a clear and articulated rationale for the most appropriate knowledge, skills and understanding for our students to acquire and by choosing exam specifications and designing programmes of study that challenge academically able students.
2. Ensuring a coherent approach to the delivery of subject curricula so that students build on prior knowledge and understanding, develop fluency and are challenged to apply prior knowledge to different contexts.
3. Carefully mapping cross-curricular links and aligning programmes of study to ensure a coherent scheduling of topics between subject areas.
4. Using assessment generally and specific strategies such as spaced practice, interleaving and retrieval practice to help embed knowledge in students’ long term memory.
5. Ensuring that students develop and apply a secure and sophisticated knowledge of language and tier 2 and 3 vocabulary,
6. Identifying and addressing those gaps in knowledge and experiences that are typical for our students, to deliver a curriculum that is relevant and appropriate.

16 - 19 Bursary Fund
The 16–19 Bursary Fund provides financial support to help students overcome financial barriers to participating fully in their education.
There are two types of bursary available:
Bursary for defined vulnerable groups For students in specific circumstances defined by the Department for Education, such as being in care, a care leaver, or receiving certain benefits in their own right.
Discretionary bursary For students experiencing financial barriers to education, based on household circumstances and the actual costs for which they need support. At Langley Grammar School, the normal financial eligibility criteria are a gross annual household income of £27,500 or less and/or the student or a sibling qualifying for Free School Meals. Exceptional financial hardship or a significant change in circumstances may also be considered.
Support may be available towards costs such as travel, food while attending school, educational visits, curriculum access devices and IT, books and course materials, essential equipment and other education-related costs.
Bursary awards are based on each student's individual circumstances and actual financial need. Meeting the eligibility criteria does not automatically guarantee an award, and the school may not always be able to meet a request in full.
Students wishing to apply should read the Information for Students and 16–19 Bursary Fund Policy before completing the online application form.
Applications for 2026–27 should be submitted by 2 October 2026. Applications received by this date will be considered together so that available funding can be distributed fairly. Applications can still be made later in the year where circumstances change, or unexpected financial hardship arises.
